title: How can an owl see without moving its eyes?

segments.text: There's a bird that, unbelievably, can't move its eyes at all, yet it sees everything around it. Which animal can do that? An owl.
Its eyes aren't round balls. They're tubes, locked in place by rings of bone, so an owl has to turn its whole head to look around.
It can twist that head up to {270|two hundred seventy} degrees. Try that yourself and the arteries in your neck could tear.
But owls have {14|fourteen} neck bones, twice as many as you, and special blood vessels with backup pools that keep blood flowing to the brain mid-twist.
Up close, though, they're nearly blind. So an owl feels its food with fine feathers around the beak.

Its real superpower is hearing. One ear sits higher than the other, and the flat disc of the face funnels sound like a satellite dish. A great gray owl can hear a mouse tunneling under deep snow, then dive in to catch it.
And you'd never hear it coming. Comb-like edges on its wing feathers break up the air, making flight nearly silent. Engineers now copy them to build quieter wind turbines.
So an owl can't move its eyes. It just moves everything else. If you enjoyed this, like and follow for more.
